Preparing for Snowy Roads.situation: Before Getting in the Car During Snowfall
Preparing for Snowy Roads.url: 雪みちの備え | おしえて！雪ナビ
advices: Shake off all the snow from the vehicle before getting in.
Remove any ice or frost from the windows completely.
Make sure to shake off all the snow from your shoes before entering the vehicle.
Check your fuel level. Since diesel fuel may freeze at low temperatures, be sure to use a cold-weather grade.

Preparing for Snowy Roads.situation: Basic Driving Operations in Snowy Conditions
Preparing for Snowy Roads.url: 雪みちの備え | おしえて！雪ナビ
advices: Tips for a Smooth Start: If you engage the clutch too abruptly when starting on a snowy road, the drive wheels may spin without traction, preventing the car from moving forward.
For manual transmission vehicles, shift into second gear; for automatic transmission vehicles, use the “creep” effect to start off gently.
Even after pulling away, applying too much power can cause the tires to spin and the vehicle to skid. If you’re driving a manual transmission vehicle, shift gears early.

Avoid Overusing the Foot Brake: Using the foot brake on snowy roads can easily cause the wheels to lock up (a condition where the tires stop spinning even while the car is moving), which may cause the rear of the vehicle to sway or increase the stopping distance.
On downhill slopes and at intersections, don’t rely solely on the foot brake; make use of engine braking instead.
Note: With manual transmission vehicles, be careful not to downshift two or three gears at once while traveling at high speed, as this can actually make the wheels more likely to lock up.

Preparing for Snowy Roads.situation: Driving on Curves and Rutted Roads
Preparing for Snowy Roads.url: 雪みちの備え | おしえて！雪ナビ
advices: Braking on Curves: As a general rule, complete any braking or downshifting on the straight section before the curve.
If you brake or downshift in the middle of a curve, the tires may suddenly lock up, causing the vehicle to veer off the road.
Driving on Rutted Roads: Driving along the ruts provides better stability for the vehicle.
To drive effectively along the ruts, hold the steering wheel loosely with a little play; this allows the car to naturally follow the ruts.
Be careful not to drive into ruts that are too deep, as this can cause the vehicle to get stuck.

Preparing for Snowy Roads.url: 雪みちの備え | おしえて！雪ナビ
advices: Turn on your headlights even during the day, and use the defroster to melt any accumulated snow.
During a blizzard, flash your hazard lights to alert following vehicles, reduce your speed, and drive carefully while using guide poles as landmarks.

Preparing for Snowy Roads.url: 雪みちの備え | おしえて！雪ナビ
advices: Do Not Apply the Parking Brake: The parking brake may freeze and fail to release.
For manual transmission vehicles, park in first gear or reverse; for automatic transmission vehicles, park in “P.”
Prop Up the Windshield Wipers: The weight of the snow may cause the wipers to bend.
Turn Off the Engine When Parking: If the exhaust pipe becomes blocked by snow, there is a severe risk of carbon monoxide poisoning.

Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.situation: Watch Out for Icy Road Surfaces (Black Ice)
Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.url: 雪害では、どのような災害が起こるのか | 首相官邸
advices: During and after snowfall, be cautious of accidents caused by icy road surfaces or reduced visibility (such as blizzards).
Watch Out for Icy Road Surfaces in These Situations: When there is 1 cm or more of snowfall, and shortly after it stops snowing (generally within 24 hours).
Watch out for black ice (road surfaces that have turned to ice)! During cold nights, early mornings, or in shaded areas, be on the lookout for black ice even if the road doesn’t appear to be frozen!
Traffic-light intersections: The road surface can become extremely slippery due to vehicles repeatedly starting and stopping.
Bridges (bridge decks): Even if the surrounding road surface isn’t frozen, the bridge deck itself may be icy.
Entrances and exits of tunnels, etc: These areas are often in the shade, so the road surface may be frozen in localized spots.

Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.situation: Tips for Driving on Icy Roads and Poor Visibility
Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.url: 雪害では、どのような災害が起こるのか | 首相官邸
advices: Be Careful When Visibility Is Poor: When there are particles suspended in the air, the amount of light reaching our eyes decreases, making it difficult to see (reduced visibility). Conditions such as blowing snow can turn the view completely white (a “whiteout”).

Driving on Hills: Shift down to the appropriate gear in advance and maintain a steady throttle. Sudden braking or downshifting can cause the rear end to swing out or the car to spin out. (Use engine braking when going downhill.)
Driving Through Curves: Slow down sufficiently before entering a curve, and maintain a moderate, steady speed while navigating the curve.

Braking: Sudden braking can cause the tires to lock up, lose traction, and prevent the vehicle from stopping. Apply the brakes gently and gradually from a distance earlier than usual to come to a stop.
Do not rely too heavily on four-wheel drive or ABS (Anti-lock Braking System); be sure to slow down sufficiently before curves and intersections.
When driving in a blizzard, turn on your headlights, slow down, and maintain a safe following distance! To make your presence known, turn on your headlights.
Watch out for snow plumes from large vehicles! Snow plumes kicked up by large vehicles can impair visibility, so turn on your windshield wipers early and slow down.
If snow accumulates on your vehicle, pull over to a safe spot to clear it off. Clear snow from your headlights, taillights, and windshield wipers in a safe spot away from the road.
Take a break if you’re tired or feel it’s unsafe to drive. If you’re tired or feel it’s dangerous, don’t stop on the road—pull over at a rest stop or parking area to rest.

Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.url: 雪害では、どのような災害が起こるのか | 首相官邸
advices: Driving on winter roads is similar to climbing in the mountains during winter, so be sure to perform pre-trip inspections and maintenance.
Carry equipment that will allow you to adequately handle various emergencies caused by sudden changes in weather and other factors.
Vehicle tools: Tire chains, jack, tow rope, tools, jumper cables, snow shovel, spare tire (winter tire), anti-skid sand, snow brush, stop sign, smoke signal.
Personal survival gear: Winter clothing, rain gear, rubber boots, work clothes, gloves, work gloves, towels, a change of clothes, a blanket, disposable hand warmers.
Emergency supplies: Shovel, emergency water, food, flag (brightly colored cloth), flashlight (with batteries), radio.

Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.url: 雪害では、どのような災害が起こるのか | 首相官邸
advices: During the winter, falls caused by snow accumulation and icy conditions occur frequently—not only in heavy snowfall areas but also in regions with little snow. Slip-and-fall accidents tend to peak between January and March.
On the white lines of crosswalks: Even if the surface appears dry, a thin layer of ice may have formed, making it slippery.
Sidewalks with vehicle traffic (parking lot entrances/exits, gas stations): Ice on the road surface may have been polished by the tires of passing vehicles, making it extremely slippery.
Bus and taxi stops: The ground may be packed down by foot traffic, making it slippery. Also, be careful of the step between the sidewalk and the road.
Slopes: It is more dangerous and easier to slip and fall when going downhill than when going uphill. Be especially careful when walking downhill.
Gaps in road heating systems: Snow and ice may not have melted in these gaps, creating uneven surfaces that can be slippery.
Take small steps: The basic technique is the “penguin walk,” where you take small steps and walk slowly and carefully.

Keep the entire sole of your shoe in contact with the ground: Shift your center of gravity slightly forward and walk with the intention of keeping the entire sole of your shoe in contact with the ground as much as possible.
Choose footwear with non-slip soles (such as rubber boots with a high coefficient of friction).
Wearing a hat and gloves in case you fall is another safety measure.
Walking with both hands in your pockets or after drinking alcohol can impair your sense of balance and is dangerous.
Be aware of snow and ice that may fall from rooftops, so keep an eye on the roofs as you walk. Be especially careful on warm days.

Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.url: 雪害では、どのような災害が起こるのか | 首相官邸
advices: Accidents during winter recreation are notably often caused by personal carelessness, lack of proper judgment, inadequate physical preparation, or insufficient equipment.
In skiing and snowboarding, accidents such as falls, slides, and collisions with people or trees occur frequently.
When people enter restricted areas on a whim without thoroughly checking the course, they often get lost or stranded. There is no guarantee of a reliable cell phone connection in mountainous areas.
In winter mountaineering, a serious situation has arisen where the number of people stranded in the mountains exceeded 500 in Reiwa 5 due to a lack of experience and inadequate preparation.
Avoid sudden, intense physical activity; instead, enjoy yourself while making a conscious effort to let your body adjust gradually. If you’re not feeling well, consider refraining from exercise.
Weather conditions at the base of the mountain can be completely different from those at the summit, so be sure to check the weather conditions and forecasts in advance.
Skiing or snowboarding beyond your ability is a recipe for accidents. Enjoy yourself within safe limits.
Sharing your mountain climbing plan and registration form with family, coworkers, and others provides a clue for a swift search and rescue operation in case of an emergency.
Submit climbing plans to the registration box at the trailhead, local government offices, prefectural police departments, or via a mountain map app.

In case of trouble, always travel in a group rather than alone, and check periodically to ensure your companions are with you. Carry a two-way radio, a cell phone, and spare batteries in preparation for emergencies.
If visibility becomes poor, do not move around; wait for the weather to clear.
If you are in distress, use your portable radio or cell phone to call 110 or 119 as needed to request rescue, and provide as much information as possible about the situation and the terrain.

If it looks like rescue will take a long time, turn off your cell phone frequently to conserve battery power, and keep it close to your body to keep it warm and prevent malfunction due to low temperatures.

If you must stay where you are, attach a marker to a tree, dig a snow cave at the base of the tree to shelter from the cold, use a hand warmer if you have one, and wait for the rescue team. Avoid moving around unnecessarily.

Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.url: 雪害では、どのような災害が起こるのか | 首相官邸
advices: An avalanche consists of the 'initiation zone', the 'runout zone', and the 'deposition zone' (where debris accumulates).
Avalanches move very quickly, and it is difficult to escape once you realize one is occurring. Check for hazardous areas and weather information regularly.
Areas Prone to Avalanches: Generally, avalanches are more likely to occur on slopes with a gradient of 30 degrees or more. Slopes between 35 and 45 degrees are considered the most dangerous.
While avalanches are less likely to occur on slopes with dense stands of tall trees, the risk increases on slopes with shrubbery or sparse vegetation (e.g., bamboo grass).
Conditions Prone to Avalanches: When temperatures are low, there is already a significant amount of snow on the ground, and a large amount of snow has fallen in a short period of time.
Conditions Prone to Avalanches: On steep slopes, especially where there are cornices or snowdrifts (areas where snow has been blown and accumulated by the wind).
Conditions Prone to Avalanches: In early spring or after rainfall, when temperatures rise due to the foehn effect.
Major Warning Signs: Snow cornices (protrusions of snow from mountain ridges or overhangs), protrusions of snow from avalanche prevention fences.
Major Warning Signs: Flattened slopes (slopes where snow has accumulated to the point that the original terrain is no longer recognizable).
Major Warning Signs: Snowballs (clumps of snow resembling balls that roll down the slope).
Major Warning Signs: Cracks (fissures in the snow that look like scratches on the slope) and Snow Wrinkles (wrinkled snow patterns resembling swollen fingertips).
Use hazard maps created and distributed by municipalities to identify dangerous areas in your region.
Check for weather information, such as “Avalanche Advisories,” “Current Warnings and Advisories”, and “Upcoming Snow” issued by the Japan Meteorological Agency.

Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.situation: What to Do During an Avalanche
Snow-Related Disasters and Accidents.url: 雪害では、どのような災害が起こるのか | 首相官邸
advices: If an Avalanche Occurs Near You: Keep your eyes on the person being swept away. Remember the point of impact and the point where they disappeared from view.
Once the avalanche has stopped, post a lookout and mark the point of impact and the point of disappearance with a pole, a tree, or another visible marker.
Immediately begin searching using an avalanche transceiver (radio) or similar device. If the person is found, dig them out immediately and administer first aid.
If you get caught in an avalanche yourself: Rescue yourself to the edge of the avalanche.
Warn the others so they don't get swept away.
Take off your baggage from your body.
Make swimming motions in the snow to try to reach the surface.
When the avalanche seems to come to a standstill, use your hands to create a free space in front of your mouth to gain room in the snow.
Since you can sometimes hear the voices of the people walking above through the snow, shout loudly as soon as you hear them.
